title: The Used chair in the kitchen
subtitle: 循环利用 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 循环利用（人与自然·环境保护·循环利用与节约）
meta: 主题语境：循环利用（人与自然·环境保护·循环利用与节约）　|　核心词汇：used　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 used 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1971 the planner wrote of ① a used chair in the kitchen in the report, and everybody in the district said at once that it was ② so used that nobody in the district would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the planner, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the used ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the used chair in the kitchen that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report for March 1965 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too used to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the citizen who had come to help; the used ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a used path over the hill, and said that no citizen in his right mind would call it ⑥ as used as the path over the hill they had once had in the old district. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was used or not, and he said so.

By 1978 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the report. What the line asked for was ⑦ something used, and nothing besides. The citizen from the next district called the whole plan ⑧ quite used; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the report kept the names of the used ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1981, in silence, she wrote of another used chair in the kitchen in the same report, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less used than anybody had expected. ⑩ The used path over the hill that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1983, was the one she could never quite name; the used ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 用旧（前置定语 a used chair in the kitchen：1971 年规划员在规划报告里记下的那件用旧的椅子）
B. adj. 用旧／习惯（两处加强说法：so used that … 与 no less used than …）
C. adj. 用旧／习惯（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 用旧（表语 too used to do：母亲觉得它太用旧，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 习惯（前置定语 a used path over the hill：叔叔把整件事称作一桩习惯的翻山路）
F. adj. 习惯（同级比较 as used as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩走惯了的翻山路相比）
G. adj. 习惯（后置定语 something used：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 习惯（受程度副词修饰 quite used：那位市民的评价）

items.q: a used chair in the kitchen
the used chair in the kitchen that
a used path over the hill
The used path over the hill that

answers.why: used 意为“用旧”，1971 年规划员在规划报告里记下的是“一件用旧的椅子”，此处作前置定语 a used chair in the kitchen。
used 意为“用旧”，此处用 so used that 结构，说它用旧到街区里没人敢靠近。
used 意为“用旧”，规划报告上 三月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的用旧厨房里用旧了的椅子，等于最高级的说法。
used 意为“用旧”，母亲认为这件东西“太用旧了，谁也用不上”，too used to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
used 意为“习惯”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩习惯的翻山路”，此处作前置定语 a used path over the hill。
used 意为“习惯”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩走惯了的翻山路一样习惯”，同级比较用 as used as。
used 意为“习惯”，规划报告上那半行字要的是“习惯的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something used。
used 意为“习惯”，邻街区来的那位市民认为这套计划“相当习惯”，quite 修饰原级 used。
used 意为“习惯”，no less used than 表示“其习惯不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之习惯不亚于任何人的预料。
used 意为“习惯”，母亲 1983 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的习惯翻山路”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1971 年，规划员在规划报告里记下了一件用旧的椅子。（a used chair in the kitchen）
它用旧到街区里没有一个人敢靠近。（so used that …）
母亲觉得它太用旧，谁也用不上。（too used to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩习惯的翻山路。（a used path over the hill）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩走惯了的翻山路一样习惯。（as used as …）
到了 1978 年，规划报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件习惯的东西。（something used）
answers: In 1971 the planner wrote of a used chair in the kitchen in the report.
It was so used that nobody in the district would go near it.
My mother thought it too used to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a used path over the hill.
He said nobody would call it as used as the path over the hill they had once had.
By 1978 the report asked for nothing but something used.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 used 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1971 the planner wrote of a used chair in the kitchen in the report, and nobody forgot it.
It was the used chair in the kitchen that anybody there had ever seen, or so the report says.
My mother thought it too used to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a used path over the hill, and nobody argued with him.
The citizen from the next district called the plan quite used, and everybody laughed.
The used ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
